# TI 2026 Context Pack

**Frozen as of:** 2026-08-10, 13:00 CEST
**Purpose:** identical input for all models in the prediction benchmark.
**Do not edit after 2026-08-12.** Any later correction goes in the changelog at the bottom.

---

## 1. Tournament

- **Event:** The International 2026 (TI15), 15th edition of the Dota 2 world championship
- **Location:** Shanghai, China. Playoffs at the Oriental Sports Center
- **Organizers:** Valve and PGL
- **Teams:** 16 (7 direct invites, 9 through regional qualifiers)
- **Group stage:** August 13–16, Swiss format. Teams play until 4 wins (advance) or 4 losses (eliminated). 8 teams reach the main event
- **Main event:** August 20–23, double elimination
- **Prize pool:** $2,786,814 total ($1,600,000 base plus 30% of supporter bundle sales)
- **Patch:** 7.41e, released July 30 alongside the pre-TI update
- **Note:** no Battle Pass this year; rewards are earned through Predictions and Fantasy

Historical note: since the Swiss format was introduced, no player has ever correctly predicted the full group stage.

---

## 2. Teams

Naming: several organizations compete under altered tags. BetBoom Team plays as **BoomBoys**, PARIVISION plays as **Team Vision** (Valve restricts gambling-related branding), the former Tundra roster now plays as **1win Team**, and L1GA TEAM qualified as **HULIGANI**. Treat these as the same rosters under different names.

### Direct invites (7)

**Team Yandex** — watson, CHIRA_JUNIOR, DM, Saksa, Malady
Won PGL Wallachia Season 7 (beat Liquid 3–2). Won BLAST Slam VII (beat LGD 3–1). Third at the Esports World Cup.

**BoomBoys / BetBoom Team** — Kiritych, gpk, MieRo, Save-, Kataomi
Won PGL Wallachia Season 8. Third at PGL Wallachia Season 7 and at BLAST Slam VII. Runner-up at the Esports World Cup, losing 1–3 to PARIVISION.

**Team Falcons** — skiter, Malr1ne, ATF, Cr1t-, Sneyking
Defending TI champions (beat Xtreme Gaming 3–2 in the TI 2025 final). Roster unchanged since. In 2026: third at PGL Wallachia Season 8, fourth at DreamLeague Season 29, seventh at the Esports World Cup.

**Team Liquid** — miCKe, Nisha, Ace, Boxi, tOfu
Added Ace and tOfu this season. Won BLAST Slam VI. Runner-up at PGL Wallachia Season 7. Top four at DreamLeague Season 28 and PGL Wallachia Season 8. Tenth at the Esports World Cup.

**1win Team** — Pure, bzm, 33, Ari, Whitemon
Invitation earned as Tundra Esports; the full roster and staff moved to 1win in June. Eleventh at the Esports World Cup, their first event under the new tag.

**Xtreme Gaming** — Ame, NothingToSay, Xxs, fy, xNova
TI 2025 runner-up. In 2026: won ESL Challenger China Season 2, fourth at DreamLeague Season 28, third at ESL One Birmingham.

**Aurora Gaming** — Nightfall, Mikoto, Ws, Mira, kaori
No title in 2026 but consistently deep runs: runner-up at DreamLeague Season 28, PGL Wallachia Season 8 and DreamLeague Season 29. Ninth at the Esports World Cup.

### Europe qualifier (4 slots)

**Team Vision / PARIVISION** — Satanic, No[o]ne, Noticed, 9Class, Dukalis
Took the second European slot, beating Virtus.pro 2–1. Won DreamLeague Season 29. Won the Esports World Cup with a 16–3 map record, beating BetBoom 3–1 in the final.

**Team Spirit** — Yatoro, Larl, Collapse, not me, rue
Took the first European slot, beating Nigma Galaxy 2–1, finishing the qualifier 6–1 on maps. Third at DreamLeague Season 29, sixth at the Esports World Cup. Two-time TI-winning organization.

**Nigma Galaxy** — SumaiL, lorenof, Davai, OmaR, GH
Took the fourth European slot, beating Yellow Submarine 2–1. Wins over Rune Eaters and NAVI in the qualifier, loss to Spirit. Eighth at the Esports World Cup.

**HULIGANI (ex-L1GA TEAM)** — ssnovv1, Mirage, Vazya, sayuw, RESPECT
Took the third European slot from the lower bracket, beating 4ikibamboni, ENJOY, then NAVI 2–1 and Virtus.pro 2–1. Limited tier-1 experience; last place at both the Esports World Cup and Games of the Future. Several players making their TI debut.

### China qualifier (2 slots)

**Vici Gaming** — shiro, Xm, Bach, XinQ, y`
Returned to professional Dota in 2026. Beat Yakutou Brothers 2–1 for the second Chinese slot. Won ESL Challenger China Season 3, top eight at PGL Wallachia Season 7. At the Esports World Cup: eliminated Falcons, reached the semifinals, finished fourth.

**Team Resilience** — Erika, EchozZ, niu, planet, zzq
Formed in April 2026. Qualified without dropping a map (2–0 over Cloud Rising, Team Refuser and Yakutou Brothers). Experienced players but very few major events as a unit.

### Southeast Asia qualifier (1 slot)

**OG** — Natsumi, Yopaj, Raven, TIMS, skem
All-Filipino roster. Top four at BLAST Slam VI. Ninth–tenth at DreamLeague Season 28 and BLAST Slam VII. Note: this lineup shares nothing with the rosters that won TI in 2018 and 2019.

### North America qualifier (1 slot)

**GamerLegion** — Ghost, RCY, Fayde, Bignum, Speeed
Won a four-team NA qualifier without dropping a map (2–0 over The Bug, 3–0 over 4 Anchors and Ilmeria). Finished outside the top eight in five of their first six tier-1 events this season; best result seventh–tenth at BLAST Slam VI.

### South America qualifier (1 slot)

**LGD Gaming** — Yuma, **Topson (stand-in)**, Wisper, Thiolicor, KJ
Chinese organization fielding the former HEROIC South American core, which finished top six at TI 2025 — the best TI result ever by a South American roster. Runner-up at BLAST Slam VII. Twelfth at the Esports World Cup, middling at 1win Essence II. Won the SA qualifier, beating PlayTime twice including 3–0 in the final.

**Late roster change:** On August 9, mid laner TaiLung was banned by PGL from TI 2026 and all future PGL events over competitive integrity issues. This is the first time a player who had already qualified for TI has been barred from competing. On August 9–10, LGD signed two-time TI champion Topson as stand-in. Topson has not played competitively since TI 2024 with Tundra Esports, where the team finished top three.

## 3. Esports World Cup 2026 — full placements

The EWC ran July 7–19 in Paris with 24 teams and a $2,000,000 prize pool. It is the most recent tier-1 event before TI and included 15 of the 16 TI participants, so it is the single best like-for-like comparison available. Placements below are the official prize-distribution brackets; teams sharing a bracket are not ranked against each other.

| Placement | TI 2026 teams in this bracket |
|---|---|
| 1st | Team Vision (as PVISION) |
| 2nd | BoomBoys (as BB Team) |
| 3rd | Team Yandex |
| 4th | Vici Gaming |
| 5th–8th | Nigma Galaxy, Team Falcons, Team Spirit |
| 9th–12th | LGD Gaming, 1win Team, Team Liquid, Aurora Gaming |
| 13th–16th | Xtreme Gaming |
| 17th–20th | GamerLegion, OG |
| 21st–24th | HULIGANI (as L1GA Team) |
| did not attend | Team Resilience |

Non-TI teams occupying the remaining slots: Rune Eaters (5th–8th), MOUZ, Virtus.pro, PlayTime (13th–16th), Level UP, REKONIX (17th–20th), Poor Rangers, Team Nemesis, IC x Insanity (21st–24th).

Format note: four round-robin groups of six, then a Survival stage, then single-elimination playoffs with Bo3 matches and a Bo5 final. Group winners went straight to the playoffs; teams placing second through fourth passed through Survival; the bottom two in each group were eliminated.

Two results worth reading carefully rather than at face value. Vici Gaming reached fourth after eliminating defending TI champions Team Falcons 2–0 in the quarterfinals. Xtreme Gaming, China's highest-profile roster, finished 13th–16th after going out in the Survival stage.

## 4. Season context

- The Esports World Cup (July 7–19, Paris) is the most recent major reference point. Podium: PARIVISION, BetBoom, Team Yandex. Vici Gaming fourth.
- Qualification route is a poor proxy for strength: Team Vision came through a qualifier and then won the EWC, while several directly invited teams finished outside the EWC top four.
- Notable absentee: Natus Vincere failed to qualify, losing to HULIGANI in the European bracket.
- Organization names no longer track region: LGD field a South American roster, OG field a Filipino roster, 1win field the former Tundra roster.

## 5. What is NOT in this pack, and why

- **No betting odds or bookmaker probabilities.** They serve as an independent baseline in the evaluation; supplying them would let models copy the answer.
- **No analyst power rankings or tiering.** Same reason — these encode someone else's prediction.
- **No group stage pairings.** Swiss round one matchups were not published at freeze time.
- **Full placement tables for the other tier-1 events of 2026.** Aggregator sources contradicted each other on several of them and could not be reconciled before the freeze. Only the Esports World Cup, verifiable against official prize distribution, is given as a table. Placements at other events appear in the team sections above as prose.

## The group stage structure

16 teams play a Swiss stage. Every team finishes in exactly one of six outcome buckets, and the number of teams in each bucket is fixed by the format:

| Bucket | Meaning | Number of teams |
|---|---|---|
| `w4_l0` | 4 wins, 0 losses | exactly 1 |
| `w4_l1` | 4 wins, 1 loss | exactly 2 |
| `w4_l2` | 4 wins, 2 losses | exactly 5 |
| `w2_l4` | 2 wins, 4 losses | exactly 5 |
| `w1_l4` | 1 win, 4 losses | exactly 2 |
| `w0_l4` | 0 wins, 4 losses | exactly 1 |

The first three buckets advance to the main event (8 teams). The last three are eliminated (8 teams).

## Your task

For each of the 16 teams, give a probability distribution over those six buckets. Separately, give each team's probability of winning the whole tournament.

Your numbers must satisfy:

- For each team, the six bucket probabilities sum to 1.0
- Across all 16 teams, the probabilities in each bucket column sum to that bucket's team count: 1, 2, 5, 5, 2, 1
- Across all 16 teams, `p_champion` sums to 1.0
- For each team, `p_champion` is at most the sum of its three advancing buckets

Use the exact team names listed in the briefing.

## Output format

Return a single JSON object and nothing else. No markdown code fences, no explanation before or after, no trailing text. The response must start with `{` and end with `}`.

```
{
  "reasoning": "Your analysis, at most 300 words. Write this first.",
  "teams": [
    {
      "team": "Team Yandex",
      "swiss": {
        "w4_l0": 0.00,
        "w4_l1": 0.00,
        "w4_l2": 0.00,
        "w2_l4": 0.00,
        "w1_l4": 0.00,
        "w0_l4": 0.00
      },
      "p_champion": 0.00
    }
  ]
}
```

The `teams` array must contain all 16 teams. Use decimals between 0 and 1, not percentages. Do not round so aggressively that the constraints break.
